VisiData: far better than Excel, and it speaks Python

The problem it solves

The first look at a data file should not need a script or a spreadsheet. Excel is slow on big files, has row limits, mangles dates and types, cannot be scripted and cannot open a JSONL file or a database. And most of the time I only want to know what is in the file.

The general idea

VisiData is a spreadsheet for the terminal. It opens CSV, Excel, Parquet, JSON, JSONL, SQLite and many database formats as the same kind of sheet, handles millions of rows, and is driven by the keyboard. You can sort, filter, group, pivot and join, and it is written in Python, so you can extend it with your own commands. That is why it is far better than Excel for my work.

Examples

vd prices.parquet
vd events.jsonl
vd database.sqlite
  • Shift-F turns the current column into a frequency table.
  • Shift-I describes the whole sheet with summary statistics.
  • Selecting rows and pressing " opens them as a new sheet.

Tips from my setup

  • Extensions written in Python. A visidatarc loads my own modules, each a small file that adds commands: 
    gA   association heatmap across all columns
zA   the strongest pairs
gO   OLS regression on the sheet
gD   a regression tree you can open node by node
B    bin a numeric column
gT   infer the column types automatically
zH   a histogram in the terminal (plotext)
     dedupe-rows, select-duplicate-rows
  • The association heatmap shows Pearson r for numeric pairs, Cramér's V for categorical ones and the variance explained (η²) for mixed pairs, which gives me a feel for a dataset before I model it.
  • A custom layout. A dark Catppuccin-style theme, the sidebar and the menu bar hidden by default, and a key (Ctrl-H) that shows the menu when I need it.
  • It goes where I go. Because it is a terminal app, I open the same sheets over SSH on the computer at home from the laptop, the iPad or the phone. See the posts about data science from anywhere and about TUIs.
  • Pair it with DuckDB. DuckDB answers the question with SQL and VisiData is how I look at the result.
